title: Reducer Hooks Patterns
description: Master useReducer and createReducer patterns for managing complex state logic in React components.

data.text: React's **useReducer** hook is the foundation for predictable state management. It mirrors Redux's reducer pattern but lives inside your component. When state transitions become complex—involving multiple sub-values or dependent updates—`useReducer` outperforms `useState` by centralizing logic and decoupling the event from the state update.

data.title: Signs your component needs a reducer:
items: The next state depends on the previous state (e.g., counters, form fields).
State logic is scattered across multiple event handlers.
You need to dispatch complex actions with payloads.
A prop or custom hook needs to trigger state changes without exposing the setter.

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: If you find yourself passing a function to setState that reads the previous state, consider switching to useReducer. It makes the dependency explicit.

data.text: Hardcoding reducers inside components limits reuse. A **reducer factory** is a function that returns a reducer pre-configured with initial state or extra behavior. This pattern lets you share reducer logic across components or extract it into a custom hook.

data.title: Avoid Mutating State
data.text: Reducers must be pure. Never mutate the state object directly—always return a new object. React relies on immutability to detect changes and trigger re-renders.

A reducer can enforce a strict state machine by returning the current state for unrecognized actions. Combined with discriminated unions, TypeScript can narrow the state shape at compile time, preventing impossible states from ever compiling.

terms.definition: A pure function (state, action) => newState that describes how state evolves in response to actions.
The function returned by useReducer that sends an action to the reducer.
A TypeScript union type where all members share a literal property (like type) used for type narrowing.
A higher-order function that returns a configured reducer, enabling reuse and composition.
The practice of never modifying state directly, instead returning new objects so React can detect changes.

data.title: Build a Form State Reducer
data.description: Create a useReducer-based form state manager that tracks values, touched fields, and errors.
steps: Define a discriminated union for actions: SET_FIELD, TOUCH_FIELD, SET_ERRORS, RESET.
Write a reducer that updates state immutably for each action type.
Return dispatch helpers like setField, touchField, and reset from a custom hook.
Test the reducer with a few action sequences to verify correctness.
data.expectedOutcome: A reusable form state hook with centralized transition logic.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: useReducer centralizes state logic, making complex transitions predictable.
Reducer factories enable reuse by pre-configuring initial state and behavior.
TypeScript discriminated unions make reducers type-safe and self-documenting.
Reducers are pure functions, so they are easy to test in isolation.
Always return new state objects—never mutate the existing state.
data.takeaway: Reach for useReducer when state transitions outgrow scattered useState setters.
